details:
HalaLoya SpaceFire Explorer is a web-based educational research prototype designed to support the exploration of fire behavior in microgravity, focusing on NASA's Burning and Suppression of Solids–II (BASS-II) investigation aboard the International Space Station.

The platform organizes available experiment information and provides interactive visual exploration of combustion-related parameters. It is intended to help students, researchers, and science enthusiasts better understand the challenges of fire behavior and fire safety in microgravity.

A central feature is the Data Provenance Engine, which distinguishes between verified information, data awaiting official confirmation, synthetic illustrative examples, and user-provided information. This approach helps prevent unverified values from being mistaken for actual NASA experimental measurements.

The project aims to improve access to space-science information, encourage responsible data exploration, and provide a foundation for future research and educational applications related to spacecraft fire safety.

The prototype was developed using web technologies, including React, TypeScript, and modern web development tools. GitHub was used for source-code management, and Cloudflare Workers was used to deploy the web application.

Super Intelligence tools, including large language models and AI coding assistance, were used to support development, code generation, troubleshooting, technical planning, and documentation. The scientific dataset itself was not represented as fully verified or replaced with AI-generated experimental measurements.

The creative aspect of the project is its combination of accessible scientific visualization, AI-assisted development, and transparent data provenance in one platform. Key considerations included scientific accuracy, source traceability, accessibility, transparency, and avoiding unsupported scientific conclusions.

The current version is an educational research prototype. Integration and validation of the complete official experimental dataset remain ongoing.
